title: Early Christian & St. Paul Heritage Route in Türkiye
seoTitle: St. Paul Trail Turkey: Early Christian Heritage Route Guide
metaDescription: Plan a private St. Paul and early Christian route in Türkiye: Antakya, Tarsus, Konya, Yalvaç, Perge, Ephesus, Cappadocia, museums, and seasons.
quickAnswer: Türkiye anchors more New Testament and early Christian heritage sites than almost anywhere outside Israel, linking Antakya (Antioch on the Orontes), Tarsus, Cappadocia, Konya (Iconium), Yalvaç (Pisidian Antioch), Perge, and Ephesus. A meaningful private driving-and-flight itinerary takes 10–14 days, ideally timed for April–May or September–October when both inland plateaus and Mediterranean ruins stay comfortable.

body.text: Which key sites (Antakya, Tarsus, Konya, Yalvaç, Perge, Ephesus, Cappadocia) anchor the route?

Following [GoTürkiye's St. Paul faith route](https://goturkiye.com/faith/in-the-footsteps-of-st-paul), the biblical arc begins in Antakya—where followers were first called Christians at the rock-cut [St. Pierre Monument Museum](https://muze.gov.tr/urun-detay?CatalogNo=WEB-STP01-01-009)—and Tarsus, St. Paul's birthplace. Moving inland and west, the route links Konya (ancient Iconium), Yalvaç (Pisidian Antioch), and coastal Perge before culminating at [UNESCO-listed Ephesus](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1018/) and the monastic valleys of [Cappadocia](https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/357/).

Note that travellers interested in trekking can also walk sections of the 500 km waymarked [St. Paul Trail](https://cultureroutesinturkey.com/st-paul-trail/) between Perge and Yalvaç (documented on [GoTürkiye's walking guide](https://goturkiye.com/walking/paul-trail)), whereas cultural travellers combine private chauffeured transfers with short domestic flights.

body.text: How many days does a meaningful private biblical itinerary take?

A well-paced private itinerary covering Tarsus, Cappadocia, Konya, Yalvaç, Perge, and Ephesus takes 10 to 14 days—allowing two to three domestic flight hops (for example, Adana/Çukurova, Kayseri, Antalya, and İzmir) so you spend your hours inside archaeological sites rather than enduring 8-hour highway transfers. If you have only 7 days, focus tightly on Ephesus, Laodicea/Hierapolis, Perge, and Yalvaç.

Check current local opening status before locking Antakya into your schedule: following the 2023 earthquakes, restoration works across Hatay mean that St. Pierre Church and regional museums operate on updated schedules that should be verified close to departure.
Which museums hold the finest early Christian artifacts?

Official Ministry of Culture & Tourism collections preserve the mosaics, inscriptions, liturgical silver, and sculpture that contextualise the ruins. Prioritize the [Ephesus Archaeological Site](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?DistId=EFS&SectionId=EFS01) paired with the Ephesus Museum in Selçuk, the rock-cut monastic chapels of [Göreme Open Air Museum](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=GRM01&DistId=GRM), the Yalvaç Museum (holding Pisidian Antioch inscriptions), and—subject to reopening status—the [Hatay Archaeology Museum](https://muze.gov.tr/muze-detay?SectionId=HTY01&DistId=HTY), renowned for its Roman and late-antique floor mosaics.

items: Verify live museum opening hours and restoration notices on muze.gov.tr before booking domestic flights.
Engage a state-licensed Turkish guide with academic grounding in New Testament history and Roman Anatolia.
Pack sturdy gripping walking shoes for polished marble streets at Ephesus and Perge, plus gravel trails at Yalvaç.
Purchase a MuseumPass Türkiye if visiting six or more state-run archaeological sites within 15 days.
Carry modest attire for active churches, chapels, and conservative Anatolian towns like Konya and Yalvaç.

body.text: When is the weather best for inland and coastal sites?

April–May and late September–October deliver the best weather across both the high Central Anatolian plateau (Cappadocia, Konya, Yalvaç at 1,000m+ elevation) and the sun-baked coastal plains of Tarsus, Perge, and Ephesus. Daytime highs hover comfortably between 18°C and 26°C with clear light and manageable crowds.

July and August routinely push coastal ruins like Ephesus and Perge past 37°C with almost no shade, while winter (December–February) brings snow and sub-zero mornings to Cappadocia and the Taurus Mountain passes between Antalya and Yalvaç.

faq.q: Do I have to hike to follow St. Paul's route in Türkiye?
faq.a: No. While the 500 km St. Paul Trail attracts long-distance trekkers between Perge and Yalvaç, most cultural travellers visit the major archaeological cities comfortably by private vehicle and domestic flights, with optional 1–2 hour scenic walks on ancient Roman roads.

faq.q: Can you combine St. Paul's route with the Seven Churches of Revelation?
faq.a: Yes. Ephesus sits on both circuits, and adding Smyrna (İzmir), Pergamon, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea (near Pamukkale) adds roughly 3–4 days to a western Anatolia itinerary.

faq.q: Is Antakya open to visitors after the 2023 earthquakes?
faq.a: Reconstruction is ongoing across Hatay. St. Pierre Monument Museum has resumed visitor access on official e-ticket schedules, while other sites and the Hatay Archaeology Museum should be verified right before travel for current hall openings.

faq.q: What is the best airport sequence for a St. Paul itinerary?
faq.a: A clean east-to-west flow flies into Çukurova International Airport (COV, serving Tarsus/Adana) or Kayseri (ASR) for Cappadocia, drives across Konya, Yalvaç, and Perge, and concludes flying out of İzmir (ADB) after Ephesus.

faq.q: Are private Mass or worship services permitted at St. Paul sites?
faq.a: Private liturgical services at active sanctuaries like the House of the Virgin Mary near Ephesus or designated chapels require advance permission from the local parish or diocese; outdoor ruins generally allow quiet group reflection only.

faq.q: How much walking is involved inside Ephesus and Perge?
faq.a: Both sites are large open-air archaeological parks requiring 2–3 hours on foot over uneven marble paving and gravel. Entering Ephesus via the Upper Gate lets you walk gently downhill toward the Grand Theatre.
